text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif unfolded his government's political and economic agenda, freezing petrol and electricity prices, increasing salary of government employees, launching a fund for debt retirement, banning lavish marriage parties and smoking in government offices, scrapping development funds for deputies and reverting to a Sunday weekly holiday.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is likely to announce his 10-member cabinet on Monday.
- President Farooq Leghari will open a three-day oil and gas summit on Tuesday.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif announced a raise of 300 rupees in the salaries of government employees of lower grades.
- To build up foreign currency reserves the government has asked the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to work out a higher rate of return on private forex deposits, sources said.
- A spokesman of the Ministry of Finance said the programme supported by resources of the International Monetary Fund under the standby agreement remains on track.
- Nawaz Sharif will meet top businessmen and industrialists of the country on February 26.
- The stocks of wheat are quite sufficient and the situation will further improve with arrival of one million tonnes of imported wheat during the next two months, an official said.
- Indian Prime Minister H.D.Deva Gowda said India was prepared to discuss minor adjustments in relation to Kashmir within the scope of the Simla agreement.
- Balochistan Chief Minister Akhtar Mengal said the National Finance Award regarding distribution of resources between the centre and the provinces was unacceptable to his province.
